theme: 3 terms on control flow and leaving code early

terms.definition: A Bool expression that Swift checks to decide which path the code takes.
terms.example: The if only runs when the condition is true, so log the value to see why it never fires.

terms.definition: A Swift statement that checks a condition and must leave the current scope if the check fails.
terms.example: Use a guard at the top of the method so we bail out when the user is not signed in.

terms.definition: A style of returning from a function as soon as a requirement fails, so the main code stays unindented.
terms.example: I rewrote the nested ifs as an early exit, and now the happy path reads straight down.

quizzes.question: Which Swift statement must leave the current scope when its check fails?
Which name describes the habit of returning as soon as a requirement is not met, keeping the main code flat?
Which expression evaluates to true or false and decides which branch of code runs?

video.title: Condition, guard & Early Exit in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 4
video.description:
Learn to talk about control flow in Swift: Condition, guard and Early Exit, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Condition - A Bool expression that Swift checks to decide which path the code takes.
guard - A Swift statement that checks a condition and must leave the current scope if the check fails.
Early Exit - A style of returning from a function as soon as a requirement fails, so the main code stays unindented.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.
